Why go: a small-group day that includes the harder-to-reach viewpoints

This 4x4 tour is capped at eight guests, which makes it calmer than the big safari trucks, and it adds two stops many island tours skip. After the Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem in the morning, you climb to Overlap Stone, a balanced boulder on the hillside above Lamai with a wide view of the east coast. The afternoon includes the second Na Muang waterfall, about 80 m high and reached by a short hike, then the Magic Garden and the viewpoint at Wat Teepangkorn.

The shared tour runs twice a week; on other days the same vehicle can be booked privately with a flexible route.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: active couples and families with children from 5 who want views and a bit of walking.
  • Choose something else if you have back problems or prefer not to hike: the jungle discovery jeep safari has easier stops.
  • Want your own pace? Book the private version and drop the stops you don't need.

Good to know

  • Overlap Stone: the climb is steep and the top is a rock ledge with no railings. Take care in wet weather.
  • Na Muang 2: the trail is uneven and muddy after rain. The pool at the top is cooler and quieter than Na Muang 1.
  • Wat Plai Laem: guests can feed the fish in the temple lake; use the fish food sold there, not bread.
  • Dress code: cover shoulders and knees for the temples.

Choosing between the shared and private version

The shared tour follows a fixed route with a German- and English-speaking guide and suits couples and small families. The private version swaps some stops for the Heaven Gate viewpoint, the Red Temple and a standing Buddha, and its start time can move to 08:30 or 09:30. Entry fees and lunch are paid separately on the private trip, so budget roughly 700 THB per person on top.
